subject: Post-call: latency validation playbook and streaming/concurrency probe plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency validation playbook and streaming/concurrency probe plan

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the p95/p99 end-to-end acceptance work.

Summary of what I took away from the session:
- Business target: sub-300ms p95 for short text generation (avg 120-200 tokens) and sub-800ms p99 under normal production traffic.
- Current provider baseline (your numbers): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s; you want alignment to a sub-300ms p95 and p99 closer to ~700–800ms if feasible.
- Streaming: you use streaming for token-by-token updates in the UI for the agent product; tail latency on the first tokens matters (startup + first-chunk time).
- Concurrency/throughput: typical burst concurrency 120–150 simultaneous requests, sustained 30–50 qps; traffic shapes include short-burst spikes (10s window) and longer daytime sustained traffic.

What Redwood proposes for the validation phase (playbook):
1) Small-scope probe (2 business days): controlled traffic from your staging environment against Redwood hosted API with traffic shaping to replicate your burst profile. Aim: validate p95 under 1x and 2x baseline concurrency.
2) Streaming-specific probe: measure time-to-first-token and steady-state per-token throughput.
3) Tail analysis: compute empirical p95/p99 of end-to-end (client->Redwood->model->client) including network egress region.
4) Failure modes: exercise model fallback and region failover to observe graceful degradation.

Data we need from you to run a representative probe:
- Representative request/response payloads (or a sanitized replay trace) — prefer sample IDs + timestamps.
- Traffic shape: qps schedule and concurrency numbers (CSV or short profile).
- Expected SLOs by endpoint (e.g., chat vs. generation) and acceptable error budget.

Proposed schedule (tentative):
- Provide artifacts by EOD Friday (2025-05-16) — sample traces + traffic profile.
- Redwood runs a baseline 2-day probe next Tue/Wed (2025-05-20/21).
- Quick sync after Day 1 to share early metrics and adjust traffic.

Attachments: I attached a simple probe template (streaming_probe_template.yaml) and a sheet to populate observed latencies (orchid_latency_profile.csv).

Next asks / decisions for you: confirm the probe window, and whether we should include an A/B comparison against your current provider endpoints or a standalone Redwood-only run first.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate logistics once you confirm.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Note: attachments referenced (streaming_probe_template.yaml, orchid_latency_profile.csv).

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchid.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@orchid.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency validation playbook and streaming/concurrency probe plan

Thanks Soojin — useful summary. We can commit to providing sanitized traces and the qps/concurrency CSV by EOD Friday. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 / p99 numbers I quoted earlier are measured end-to-end from our browser clients in us-west; they include our client-side processing and occasional CDN hops. We will provide both raw server-side logs and client-observed numbers.
- For streaming: our UI treats the first 4 tokens as high-importance (visible to the user immediately). If time-to-first-token is >200ms the UX degrades noticeably.
- We want the initial probe to include a head-to-head comparison: one run routed to our incumbent provider and one run to Redwood, both with identical traffic shaping. This helps our infra team quantify delta quickly.

One more operational ask: will Redwood include JVM-level and model-inference timestamps or a tracing header we can stitch to our logs? If not, we’ll need a mapping plan.

We’ll attach the traces and the traffic profile in a follow-up email (sensitive data scrubbed). Confirm the exact API endpoints and any auth tokens you need for staging.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering (Platform)
OrchidAI
alex.johnson@orchid.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchid.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency validation playbook and streaming/concurrency probe plan

Alex — quick technical notes from my side that will make the head-to-head apples-to-apples: 

- Please include request sizes (token counts) distribution in the CSV; Redwood runtime selects kernels based on sequence length and we need representative percentiles.
- Provide sample trace IDs and timestamps so we can correlate Redwood logs with your client logs. We support distributed-tracing headers (traceparent) — if you can propagate those in the probe that will be ideal.
- For streaming: include the chunk size you use (e.g., 16 tokens per chunk or adaptive). Time-to-first-token depends on both model latency and chunk flushing.
- If you expect encrypted payloads or specific TLS pinning, call that out — otherwise we'll use standard TLS to your staging endpoint.

Operational plan suggestion: run the head-to-head in three phases so we can iterate fast:
1) Dry run (1 hour) to validate instrumentation and clocks.
2) Baseline run (6 hours) at nominal traffic.
3) Stress probe (4 hours) exercising burst windows and failover.

I can own the dry-run orchestration; Soojin, can you lock the staging endpoints and tokens and confirm times?

- Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orchid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency validation playbook and streaming/concurrency probe plan — confirmed window and next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for the fast turnaround. Confirming we received your note and will proceed with the head-to-head. Finalized items below: 

Confirmed artifacts from OrchidAI (expected by EOD 2025-05-16):
- sanitized server traces (CSV)
- client-observed latencies (browser)
- request size distribution (tokens) and streaming chunk settings
- staging endpoints + auth token (time-limited)

Probe schedule (locked):
- Dry run (instrumentation validate): Tue 2025-05-20 08:00–09:00 PT
- Baseline run: Tue 2025-05-20 09:15–15:15 PT (6 hours)
- Stress probe: Wed 2025-05-21 09:00–13:00 PT (4 hours)

Deliverables and metrics we will report back within 24 hours after each run:
- end-to-end p50/p95/p99 (client-observed and server-observed)
- time-to-first-token distribution and median
- throughput and concurrency vs observed latency curves
- failure-mode behaviors and suggestions for mitigations (caching, batching, chunk sizing)

Log correlation: we support W3C traceparent headers; please include those in your replay traces. If clock skew is a concern, add server-side monotonic timestamps — Ben will coordinate trace stitching.

Next action items:
- Alex: drop the artifacts and a link to the staging credentials into the Drive folder (link in metadata) or share via secure transfer.
- Ben: I’ll coordinate the dry-run and share an instrumentation checklist before Tuesday.
- Marissa: can you scope a brief internal runbook for the customer facing dashboard we'll share (one-pager) — target EOD Wed.

If anything changes on your side (window/tokens), flag immediately. Looking forward to validating and giving you a clear delta vs your current provider.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.inference.com
